chunks: In the dream, that stolen day still had guilt clinging to it, like salt I couldn’t rinse off. I could feel how badly I wanted it to be harmless.
Kai’s warning in the lineup wasn’t cruel, and I don’t resent him for it. He was just naming the water as he saw it.
But waiting was my choice. I stayed back until the wave was mine, not because he told me to, but because I knew it.
That synthetic dream showed me something quiet: I don’t have to steal the moment to belong in it. I can wait, and still rise when it comes.
